notes.summary: Polity gives about 2 to 4 questions per paper. Most ask an Article number (which Article says what), a source (which country a feature came from), a schedule or amendment, or a fact about Parliament, the President or the courts. Learn the article table well: the same 40 articles cover most questions.

concepts.title: Making of the Constitution
concepts.body:
• The Constituent Assembly was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946). First meeting: 9 December 1946 (temporary chairman Sachchidananda Sinha). Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected its permanent president on 11 December 1946.
  • Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 (adopted 22 January 1947). It became the Preamble.
  • Drafting Committee (29 August 1947): chairman Dr B.R. Ambedkar. B.N. Rau was the constitutional adviser.
  • Adopted on 26 November 1949 (now Constitution Day). Came fully into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day). It took about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.
  • National Anthem and National Song adopted on 24 January 1950, the last day of the Assembly.
  • The original Constitution had a Preamble, 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. It was handwritten by Prem Behari Narain Raizada.

concepts.title: Sources of the Constitution
concepts.body:
SourceFeatures borrowed
Government of India Act 1935Federal scheme, office of Governor, emergency provisions, public service commissions, judiciary set-up (the largest source)
BritainParliamentary government, rule of law, single citizenship, cabinet system, writs, two houses, law-making procedure
USAFundamental Rights, judicial review, independent judiciary, impeachment of the President, removal of judges, post of Vice-President
IrelandDirective Principles, nomination to Rajya Sabha, method of electing the President
CanadaFederation with a strong centre, residuary powers with the centre, Governors appointed by the centre, advisory role of the Supreme Court
AustraliaConcurrent List, freedom of trade, joint sitting of Parliament
Former USSRFundamental Duties; ideals of social, economic and political justice
FranceRepublic; liberty, equality, fraternity
Germany (Weimar)Suspension of Fundamental Rights in an emergency
South AfricaAmendment procedure, election of Rajya Sabha members
Japan'Procedure established by law'

concepts.title: Preamble and parts
concepts.body:
The Preamble declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic and promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. 'Socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), the only change to the Preamble. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) the Supreme Court held the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.

PartSubjectArticles
IUnion and its territory1 to 4
IICitizenship5 to 11
IIIFundamental Rights12 to 35
IVDirective Principles36 to 51
IV-AFundamental Duties51A
VThe Union (President, Parliament, Supreme Court, CAG)52 to 151
VIThe States152 to 237
VIIIUnion Territories239 to 242
IXPanchayats243 to 243-O
IX-AMunicipalities243-P to 243-ZG
IX-BCo-operative societies243-ZH to 243-ZT

concepts.title: Schedules, states and citizenship
concepts.body:
ScheduleContent
1stStates and union territories
2ndSalaries of President, Governors, judges, CAG and others
3rdForms of oaths
4thRajya Sabha seats for states and UTs
5thScheduled Areas and tribes
6thTribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
7thUnion, State and Concurrent lists
8thLanguages (22 now; 14 at first)
9thLaws protected from court review (added by 1st Amendment, 1951)
10thAnti-defection (52nd Amendment, 1985)
11thPanchayats, 29 subjects (73rd Amendment)
12thMunicipalities, 18 subjects (74th Amendment)

Languages added to the 8th Schedule: Sindhi (1967); Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali (1992); Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali (2003).

New states: Article 3 lets Parliament form new states. Andhra (1953) was the first linguistic state. Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura became states in 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971. Sikkim 1975; Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa 1987; Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand 2000; Telangana 2014. In 2019, Jammu and Kashmir became two UTs. Today India has 28 states and 8 union territories.

Citizenship: Articles 5 to 11; Citizenship Act 1955. Ways to get it: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory. India has single citizenship.

concepts.title: Fundamental Rights (Articles 12 to 35)
concepts.body:
ArticleRight
14Equality before law and equal protection of laws
15No discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth; 15(2) access to shops, restaurants, wells, roads and public places
16Equal opportunity in public jobs
17Abolition of untouchability
18Abolition of titles
19Six freedoms: speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession
20Protection in respect of conviction (no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination)
21Life and personal liberty (includes privacy, from the Puttaswamy case 2017)
21AFree and compulsory education for ages 6 to 14 (86th Amendment, 2002)
22Protection against arbitrary arrest
23Ban on human trafficking and forced labour
24No child below 14 in factories, mines or hazardous work
25 to 28Freedom of religion
29 to 30Cultural and educational rights of minorities
32Right to constitutional remedies: Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution

Five writs (Supreme Court under Art 32, High Courts under Art 226): habeas corpus (produce the body), mandamus (we command), prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto (by what authority). The Right to Property was removed from Part III by the 44th Amendment (1978) and is now a legal right under Article 300A. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even in an emergency.

concepts.title: Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties
concepts.body:
Directive Principles (Part IV, Articles 36 to 51) come from Ireland. Courts cannot enforce them (Article 37), but they aim at a welfare state.

ArticleDirective
39Adequate livelihood; equal pay for equal work; resources for the common good
39AEqual justice and free legal aid (added 1976)
40Organise village panchayats (Gandhian)
41Right to work, education and public help
42Just working conditions and maternity relief
43Living wage; cottage industries (Gandhian)
43AWorkers in the management of industries (added 1976)
44Uniform Civil Code
45Early childhood care up to age 6
46Education and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections (Gandhian)
47Nutrition, public health, prohibition of intoxicating drinks (Gandhian)
48Modern agriculture and animal husbandry; ban on cow slaughter (Gandhian)
48AProtect environment, forests and wildlife (added 1976)
49Protect monuments
50Separate the judiciary from the executive
51International peace and security

Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A) came from the former USSR. Added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the advice of the Swaran Singh Committee; 10 duties at first. The 11th duty (parents to give children aged 6 to 14 a chance of education) came with the 86th Amendment (2002).

concepts.title: Parliament
concepts.body:
• Article 79: Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha.
  • Lok Sabha: maximum 550 elected members; 543 at present; term 5 years; minimum age 25. First Speaker: G.V. Mavalankar. First woman Speaker: Meira Kumar.
  • Rajya Sabha: maximum 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated for literature, science, art and social service under Article 80); a permanent house, one-third retire every 2 years; member term 6 years; minimum age 30. The Vice-President is its chairman.
  • Joint sitting (Article 108), presided by the Speaker; held three times (Dowry Prohibition 1961, Banking Service Commission Repeal 1978, POTA 2002).
  • Money Bill (Article 110): only in Lok Sabha; the Speaker decides; Rajya Sabha can hold it for only 14 days.
  • Budget is the Annual Financial Statement (Article 112). Consolidated Fund (266), Contingency Fund (267), Appropriation Bill (114).
  • Gap between two sessions must not exceed 6 months (Article 85). Quorum: one-tenth of members.
  • Question Hour is the first hour; Zero Hour (after it) is an Indian practice.
Financial committeeFact
Public Accounts CommitteeStarted 1921; 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha); chairman from the opposition by convention; examines CAG reports
Estimates CommitteeFirst set up after independence in 1950; 30 members, all from Lok Sabha
Committee on Public Undertakings1964; 22 members

concepts.title: President, Prime Minister and Governor
concepts.body:
ArticleSubject
52, 53There shall be a President; executive power of the Union
54, 55Election of the President by elected MPs and elected MLAs (including Delhi and Puducherry), by proportional representation with single transferable vote
61Impeachment of the President
63, 66Vice-President, elected by all members of both Houses
72Pardoning power of the President
74Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
75PM appointed by the President; ministers' size capped at 15% of Lok Sabha (91st Amendment)
76Attorney General of India
123President's ordinances
153 to 167Governor (153), Governor's pardon (161), Chief Minister (164), Advocate General (165)
213Governor's ordinances
  • Minimum age for President and Vice-President: 35. The President resigns to the Vice-President; the Vice-President resigns to the President.
  • First President: Dr Rajendra Prasad (the only one with two full terms). First Vice-President: Dr S. Radhakrishnan. First woman President: Pratibha Patil. Droupadi Murmu is the first tribal President. N. Sanjiva Reddy was elected unopposed.

concepts.title: Supreme Court and High Courts
concepts.body:
• Article 124: Supreme Court. Started with a Chief Justice and 7 judges; now a Chief Justice and up to 33 other judges. Judges retire at 65; High Court judges at 62. Removal by Parliament with a special majority for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
  • Article 129: court of record. Article 131: original jurisdiction (disputes between the centre and states). Article 137: review. Article 141: its law binds all courts. Article 143: advisory opinion to the President.
  • High Courts: Article 214; writs under Article 226 (wider than Art 32, as it also covers legal rights); Article 231: one High Court for two or more states. The oldest High Courts (1862) are Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.
  • First Chief Justice of India: H.J. Kania. First woman Supreme Court judge: M. Fathima Beevi (1989).
  • Public Interest Litigation was started by Justices P.N. Bhagwati and V.R. Krishna Iyer. Lok Adalats work under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
CaseHeld
Golaknath (1967)Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights (later reversed)
Kesavananda Bharati (1973)Basic structure doctrine
Maneka Gandhi (1978)Wide reading of Article 21
Minerva Mills (1980)Balance of Fundamental Rights and DPSP is basic structure
Indra Sawhney (1992)27% OBC quota upheld; 50% ceiling; creamy layer
S.R. Bommai (1994)Limits on President's rule (Article 356)
Vishaka (1997)Guidelines on sexual harassment at work
K.S. Puttaswamy (2017)Privacy is a Fundamental Right

concepts.title: Centre-state relations and emergency
concepts.body:
• Seventh Schedule: Union List (defence, foreign affairs, railways, banking), State List (police, public order, public health, agriculture), Concurrent List (education, forests, marriage, criminal law). Originally 97, 66 and 47 subjects.
  • Residuary powers lie with the Union (Article 248), as in Canada.
  • Article 249: Rajya Sabha can let Parliament make laws on a State List subject in the national interest.
  • Article 263: Inter-State Council. Zonal Councils come from the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (not the Constitution).
  • Article 280: Finance Commission, every five years, shares taxes between centre and states.
EmergencyArticleUsed
National emergency (war, external aggression, armed rebellion)3521962, 1971, 1975
President's rule in a state356Many times; first in Punjab, 1951
Financial emergency360Never

The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352.

concepts.title: Panchayats and municipalities
concepts.body:
• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) suggested a three-tier panchayat system: village, block, district. The first panchayati raj was started at Nagaur, Rajasthan, on 2 October 1959.
  • Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) suggested two tiers.
  • 73rd Amendment (1992): panchayats, Part IX, 11th Schedule (29 subjects). In force on 24 April 1993, now National Panchayati Raj Day.
  • 74th Amendment (1992): municipalities, Part IX-A, 12th Schedule (18 subjects).
  • One-third of seats reserved for women; term 5 years; minimum age 21; State Election Commission (Article 243K) holds the elections; State Finance Commission every 5 years (243-I).
  • PESA Act 1996 extended panchayats to Fifth Schedule (tribal) areas.

concepts.body:
Article 368 gives the procedure. Some changes need a simple majority, most need a special majority of Parliament, and federal changes also need half the state legislatures.

varieties.name: Making and sources of the Constitution
varieties.how: Learn the key dates (9 Dec 1946, 26 Nov 1949, 26 Jan 1950) and the source table. Ask: is the feature about rights (USA), directives (Ireland), duties (USSR), lists or trade (Australia) or a strong centre (Canada)?

example.q: The idea of residuary powers with the centre was taken from the constitution of:
steps: A federation with a strong centre is the Canadian model.
Canada keeps residuary powers with the centre, and so does India (Article 248).

varieties.name: Preamble, parts, schedules and citizenship
varieties.how: Learn the parts with their article ranges and the 12 schedules in order. For state formation, learn the year and the Act.

example.q: Which schedule deals with the anti-defection law?
steps: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the anti-defection law.
It was placed in the Tenth Schedule.

varieties.name: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and duties
varieties.how: Memorise Articles 14 to 32 one by one. For DPSP, tag the Gandhian ones (40, 43, 46, 47, 48) and the ones added in 1976 (39A, 43A, 48A).

example.q: Which Article promotes equal justice and free legal aid?
steps: Free legal aid is a Directive Principle added by the 42nd Amendment.
It is Article 39A.

varieties.name: Parliament
varieties.how: Learn the numbers (550, 250, 12 nominated, ages 25 and 30) and the money articles (110, 112, 266, 267). For committees, know size, house and year.

example.q: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses?
steps: Joint sitting is under Article 108.
It is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

varieties.name: President, PM and Governor
varieties.how: Pair each office with its Article and with who elects, appoints or removes it.

example.q: Who elects the Vice-President of India?
steps: The President's electoral college includes MLAs.
The Vice-President is elected only by members of both Houses of Parliament (elected and nominated).
example.answer: Members of both Houses of Parliament

varieties.name: Supreme Court and High Courts
varieties.how: Remember Article 32 for the Supreme Court and 226 for High Courts, the retirement ages, and one line for each landmark case.

example.q: Which Article lets a High Court issue writs?
steps: The Supreme Court issues writs under Article 32.
High Courts issue them under Article 226.

varieties.name: Centre-state relations and local government
varieties.how: Ask which list a subject is in, and which article covers which emergency (352, 356, 360). For local bodies, link 73rd to panchayats and 74th to municipalities.

example.q: The first panchayati raj system in India was started at:
steps: It followed the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee.
Nehru inaugurated it at Nagaur, Rajasthan, on 2 October 1959.

varieties.name: Constitutional and other bodies
varieties.how: Learn body and Article as a pair. First check whether the body is in the Constitution at all (NITI Aayog and NHRC are not).

example.q: Which body is set up under Article 280?
steps: Article 280 falls in Part XII (Finance).
It creates the Finance Commission.

varieties.name: Constitutional amendments
varieties.how: Learn the 15 key amendments by number, year and change. Group them: 42nd and 44th (Emergency era), 73rd and 74th (local bodies), 101st to 106th (recent).

example.q: Which amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18?
steps: This was done in 1989.
It was the 61st Amendment.

varieties.name: Laws and Acts
varieties.how: Learn the Act and its year, and for new laws, which old law each one replaced.

example.q: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 replaced which law?
steps: Sakshya means evidence.
So it replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

tips: Articles 14 to 18 are equality, 19 to 22 freedom, 23 to 24 against exploitation, 25 to 28 religion, 29 to 30 culture and education, 32 remedies.
Emergency trio: 352 national, 356 state, 360 financial (the bigger the number, the rarer: 360 never used).
Source hook: Rights from the USA, Directives from Ireland, Duties from the USSR, Concurrent List from Australia, strong centre from Canada.
73 is for villages (panchayats) and 74 for towns (municipalities): 11th Schedule has 29 subjects, 12th has 18.
Age ladder: 21 panchayat, 25 Lok Sabha and MLA, 30 Rajya Sabha and MLC, 35 President, Vice-President and Governor.
Retirement: 65 for Supreme Court judges and CAG (or 6 years), 62 for High Court judges.
traps: Article 360 is financial emergency, not national emergency (352).
The 42nd Amendment changed the Preamble; the 44th removed the Right to Property.
The Vice-President is elected by all MPs, including nominated ones, but nominated MPs do not vote for the President.
Dr Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly; Dr Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
NITI Aayog, NHRC and the CBI are not constitutional bodies; the Finance Commission and Election Commission are.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.solution:
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
Memory hook: 17 = 'end of untouchability' — the middle of the equality block 14–18.

questions.q: The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the constitution of:
questions.solution:
Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment, inspired by the constitution of the former USSR.
Memory hook: Soviet = duty to the state.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.
Memory hook: Ambedkar = Architect (both start with A).

questions.q: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called which Article the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) lets a person go directly to the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights.
Memory hook: 32 teeth protect the mouth; Article 32 protects your rights.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.solution:
The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 (in force 1989) reduced the voting age to 18.
Memory hook: say it as one line — 'Sixty-one made eighteen vote'.

questions.q: The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
questions.solution:
The Concurrent List (and joint sitting of Parliament) was borrowed from Australia. Canada gave the idea of a federation with a strong Centre.
Memory hook: Australia = All share (Concurrent).

questions.q: Which amendment added the words 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble?
questions.solution:
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity'. It is called the 'mini-constitution'.
Memory hook: 42 = the 'mini-constitution' that touched even the Preamble.

Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency. National Emergency is Article 352.
Memory hook: 360° covers all the money — Financial Emergency.
